newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN SHARES NEAR RECORDS AS WALL STREET BOOSTS.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN SHARES NEAR RECORDS AS WALL STREET BOOSTS.

text.p: The overnight rally on Wall Street and continued gains on Thursday pushed German shares back toward record territory on Thursday afternoon.
News of a U.K. interest rate rise added to the positive feeling in Frankfurt, as dealers bet that this move marked the end of rate increases in Britain.

"If this had been a U.S. rate rise, people would have got scared," said one dealer. "But this was neutral to positive for the market." The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 94.29 points at 4,458.54 at 1345 GMT, just off its all-time high of 4,477.70 points.
Earlier the DAX index ended the bourse session at mid-afternoon at 4,414.35 points, buoyed in particular by a strong performance by utility and bank shares.
Dealers said volumes had picked up clearly after lagging on Wednesday, as fears about an imminent rise in German interest rates appeared to be ebbing.
At the same time, some dealers warned that many market participants remained sidelined, capping the potential for a sustained breach of old records in the short term.
Financial shares, booming in recent weeks as signs emerged of more sectoral consolidation, were in centre stage.
Insurer Allianz AG was up nearly four percent at 462.50 marks, while Deutsche Bank AG was up 2.60 marks at 120.25 marks.
Heavyweight engineering company Siemens AG also helped drag the index higher with a rise of 4.10 marks to 128.55 marks.
Utilities, which dealers noted have lagged in recent weeks, were performing firmly. Viag AG was up 12.5 marks at 796.50 marks.
Sportswear group Adidas AG surged 7.70 marks to 230.00 marks after reporting results on Wednesday.
Paribas Capital Markets raised Adidas to buy from no action, citing the outlook for Adidas to keep up high double-digit gains in sales and operating profit for 1997.
Commerzbank raised its six-month price target for the share to 250 marks.
The apparent slowdown in the dollar's advance against the mark was underpinning share gains.

The dollar appeared to calm against the deutschemark and traded well below this week's highs of 1.89 marks on Thursday at around 1.875 marks, easing the risk that the Bundesbank will tighten monetary policy soon to rescue the German currency.
